title: In matched Cycle 24 and 25 months, F10.7 is higher at fixed HMI sunspot area
abstract: We test whether the Cycle 25 emission excess remains when direct sunspot area replaces sunspot number. Common-day monthly fits in January 2011 to November 2013 and January 2022 to November 2024 give a 10.04% rise in F10.7 at fixed HMI area (conditional 95% limits 4.55 to 15.74). Measured Mg II rises by 1.62% (0.55 to 2.72), while sunspot number changes by 0.91% (-8.36 to 11.24). Phase, source, observing-time and later-window tests retain an emission rise. Ground area gives a similar emission constraint but differs from HMI by about 6%. Thus a count change alone is not sufficient under stable area and emission scales and the fitted response. The physical cause remains open. We also find exact duplicate rows in the 2025 Mandal group-file snapshot; raw row counts would create a false near-doubling of later group counts. We give a repair rule and audit. Code, estimates, figures, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. External observations and repaired record-level tables stay outside the publication. Limited overlap, model error and possible scale drift prevent a solar cause from being proved.

display.caption: Common-day Cycle 24 and 25 fits with reference overlap. Points show percentage changes and conditional 95% residual-block intervals. Each panel has a separate overlap sample. Total-index Mg II changes are not excess-emission fractions.
